headline: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal awards top buyers and sellers on GEM platform at the 10th Anniversary celebrations of GEM
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal awards top buyers and sellers on GEM platform at the 10th Anniversary celebrations of GEM

Shri Goyal Calls Lauds GeM Platform for Making Public Procurement Efficient, Inclusive Transparent and Competitive

GeM’s Next Decade to Focus on Last-Mile Access, AI, Integration, Credit, Sustainability and University Outreach: Shri Goyal

GeM Launches Customised ‘My Stamp’ to Mark 10th Foundation Day

GeM Introduces Nationwide Short Code “14550” for Helpdesk Services

10 AUG 2026 9:49PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal called for a new, user-friendly and AI-enabled platform to make public procurement more efficient, cost-effective, transparent and competitive. Addressing the 10th Foundation Day celebration of Government e Marketplace (GeM) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, Shri Goyal said the new platform would help buyers and sellers make more intelligent use of the procurement process and the latest technologies.

Outlining five priorities for the decade ahead, Shri Goyal emphasised strengthening last-mile access through GeM’s Suvidha Kendras by expanding registration, cataloguing, training and grievance redressal across districts; deeper use of Artificial Intelligence for price intelligence, price sanity and marketplace integrity; integration of States, public enterprises, panchayats and cooperatives into a seamless national procurement ecosystem; greater focus on credit and sustainability through scaling GeM Sahay and TReDS linkages and mainstreaming sustainable procurement; and university outreach to bring young innovators and new buyers onto the platform.

The occasion was also graced by Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Shri S. Krishnan, and Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, along with senior government officials, buyers, sellers, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders.

The celebrations brought together government buyers, sellers, entrepreneurs, policymakers and other stakeholders who have been part of GeM’s journey since its inception in 2016. The occasion reflected on the platform’s growth as well as the contribution of enterprises and individuals whose participation has given scale and meaning to this transformation.

Launched on 9 August 2016 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, inspired by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for technology-enabled, transparent and efficient governance, GeM has evolved from a digital marketplace into a unified public procurement platform connecting government buyers and enterprises across the country.

GeM has a community of more than 25 lakh sellers and over 1.37 lakh buyer organisations. The platform has facilitated cumulative procurement of over ₹20 lakh crore through more than 3.78 crore orders. It now has 12.28 lakh Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), which have fulfilled orders worth more than ₹9 lakh crore, accounting for 45.6 per cent of cumulative GMV. More than 2.24 lakh women-led MSEs have fulfilled over 50 lakh orders valued at more than ₹1 lakh crore, while 42,242 startups have secured orders worth more than ₹65,633 crore.

Technology has remained central to GeM’s evolution. Digital processes have strengthened transparency and traceability, while integration with government digital systems has made procurement and related transactions more seamless.

Welcoming the gathering, Chief Executive Officer, GeM, Shri Mihir Kumar, said, “We are proud of how far we have come. Yet what truly defines GeM is not only the scale we have achieved, but the spirit with which we continue to improve—listening, refining and remaining responsive to the needs of those who use the platform.”

The Foundation Day programme showcased GeM’s evolution through the screening of the GeM 10-year journey film, capturing its transformation and growing impact across the country.

A customised My Stamp was also launched to commemorate the milestone. The stamp recognises GeM’s contribution to digital governance, Ease of Doing Business, promotion of Indian enterprises and inclusive economic growth, while symbolising its commitment to building a transparent, efficient and future-ready public procurement ecosystem aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

GeM also launched a dedicated nationwide five-digit short code “14550” for its Helpdesk. The new number provides a simple and recognisable communication identity for GeM and is virtually mapped to the existing Helpdesk infrastructure to ensure continuity of services. It will make it easier for buyers, sellers and other stakeholders to access support and identify official GeM communications.

The Foundation Day celebrations also recognised and felicitated exemplary buyers from Central Ministries and Departments, State Government Departments and sellers for their contribution to strengthening and advancing India’s public procurement ecosystem.

As GeM enters its second decade, the focus is shifting from expanding the platform to multiplying its impact. The next phase will focus on deeper technology adoption, wider participation, greater Ease of Doing Business, stronger procurement intelligence, faster processes and continued efforts to deliver greater value for public money.

For Indian enterprises, the objective is to make government procurement an even more accessible and predictable market, while for buyers, the focus is to provide a smarter, more efficient and increasingly data-driven procurement experience.

As India advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat, GeM aspires to further transform public procurement in India and position the country’s digital public procurement model as a trusted global benchmark.

headline: Prevention and Healthy Lifestyles Must Go Hand in Hand with Disease Treatment : Shri Prataprao Jadhav
fullText:
Prevention and Healthy Lifestyles Must Go Hand in Hand with Disease Treatment : Shri Prataprao Jadhav

India’s Traditional Knowledge Systems Must Be Integrated with Modern Scientific Research and Evidence: Shri Prataprao Jadhav

Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav chairs Fifth Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting of Ministry of Ayush

Committee deliberates on strengthening Yoga and Naturopathy through education, research, quality standards and wider community access

10 AUG 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, chaired the Fifth Meeting of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Ayush in New Delhi today. The meeting focused on “Yoga and Naturopathy” and deliberated on their growing relevance in preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles, rehabilitation and holistic well-being.

Addressing the Committee, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that Yoga and Naturopathy hold a distinct place in India's rich knowledge tradition and offer holistic, drug-free approaches focused on health promotion and overall well-being. He said Yoga contributes to physical, mental and emotional well-being, while Naturopathy emphasises nutrition, lifestyle modification, natural therapies and the body's inherent healing capacity.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the growing burden of non-communicable diseases, stress and mental health challenges associated with modern lifestyles. He emphasised that alongside treatment of diseases, there is a strong need to focus on disease prevention and promotion of healthy lifestyles. He said Yoga and Naturopathy can support healthy ageing, rehabilitation, mental health, stress and pain management, maternal and child health and wellness. Highlighting the importance of healthy ageing, he said that with India’s elderly population increasing, maintaining physical activity, mental health, mobility, independence and quality of life is essential, and Yoga and Naturopathy can play an important role in supporting healthy and active ageing.

Shri Jadhav said that the Government is strengthening the institutional ecosystem for Yoga and Naturopathy through the Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), Yoga Certification Board (YCB), National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN) and Naturopathy Registration Board (NRB). He highlighted their role in education, training, certification, research, healthcare, quality assurance and professional standardisation, and said that the establishment of the Naturopathy Registration Board is an important step towards strengthening registration and quality standards in Naturopathy.

Emphasising the need to integrate India’s traditional knowledge systems with modern scientific research and evidence, Shri Jadhav said, “Tradition is our strength, science is its evidence, and quality is our priority.” He stressed that Yoga and Naturopathy should complement modern medicine, with greater focus on prevention, health promotion, lifestyle modification, rehabilitation and wellness.

A detailed presentation was made by Ms. Alarmelmangai D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, covering the institutional, educational, research and outreach ecosystem of Yoga and Naturopathy. The presentation highlighted 22 CCRYN units nationwide, 100+ universities offering Yoga courses, 5,000+ Yoga centres, 113 accredited institutions and 29 accredited Personnel Certification Bodies, along with India’s growing research base of 10,500+ peer-reviewed, PubMed-indexed publications and initiatives in research collaboration, digital outreach, wellness tourism and employment generation.

Members of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee present at the meeting included Dr. Swami Sachidanand Hari Sakshi, Shri Ashtikar Patil Nagesh Bapurao, Shri Khalilur Rahman, Shri Nilesh Dnyandev Lanke and Shri Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu from Lok Sabha; Shri Ghanshyam Tiwari, Shri Sadanand Mhalu Shet Tanavade, Shri Babubhai Jesangbhai Desai and Dr. Laxmikant Bajpayee from Rajya Sabha; and Permanent Special Invitees Shri Krishna Prasad Tenneti and Smt. Jyotsna Charandas Mahant from Lok Sabha, and Smt. Dharmshila Gupta and Smt. Renuka Chowdhury from Rajya Sabha. During the deliberations, Members of Parliament and expert members unanimously agreed on the need for a unified regulatory mechanism for education in Yoga and Naturopathy.

Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush; Dr. Mukhtar Ahmad Qasmi, Advisor (Unani), Ministry of Ayush; Yoga and Naturopathy experts and stakeholders; and other senior officials of the Ministry were also present at the meeting.

The Ministry outlined the following seven key priority areas for strengthening Yoga and Naturopathy in the coming years :

Strengthening education and institutional infrastructure in Yoga and Naturopathy.

Promoting scientific research and evidence generation in both systems.

Strengthening certification, accreditation and professional standards in Yoga.

Enhancing registration, quality assurance and standardisation in Naturopathy.

Expanding community-level access to Yoga- and Naturopathy-based preventive and wellness services.

Promoting Yoga and Naturopathy as key components of wellness tourism and medical value travel in India.

Taking India’s Yoga and Naturopathy traditions to the global stage, backed by scientific evidence and quality standards.

The meeting reaffirmed the importance of continued collaboration between the Ministry, Parliament and stakeholders in strengthening Yoga and Naturopathy as evidence-based, accessible systems of preventive healthcare, in line with the vision of a Healthy India and Viksit Bharat–2047.

headline: Department of Health Research- Indian Council of Medical Research (DHR-ICMR) to Host S.H.I.N.E. Nationwide, Inviting School Students to Spend a Day as Scientist
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Department of Health Research- Indian Council of Medical Research (DHR-ICMR) to Host S.H.I.N.E. Nationwide, Inviting School Students to Spend a Day as Scientist

S.H.I.N.E. 2026: Science, Health and Innovation for NextGen Explorers

DHR-ICMR’s S.H.I.N.E. returns for its second edition, expanding nationwide school outreach

Two-day S.H.I.N.E. 2026 to bring students face-to-face with scientists at 83 locations across India

Around 30,000 students from Grades 9–12 to experience ICMR research, laboratories and scientific innovation

10 AUG 2026 8:59PM by PIB Delhi

Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for students to “spend one day as a scientist,” the Department of Health Research- Indian Council of Medical Research (DHR-ICMR) is set to organise the second edition of S.H.I.N.E. – Science, Health and Innovation for NextGen Explorers, a nationwide school outreach initiative, on 11–12 August 2026.

The two-day programme will be hosted across 83 locations nationwide, including ICMR institutes, DHR-Model Rural Health Research Units (MRHRUs), and affiliated field units, providing school students with an opportunity to engage with scientists, explore scientific research, and experience the world of health and innovation firsthand.

The Secretary, Department of Health Research and Director General, ICMR, Dr. Rajiv Bahl welcomed participating students and encouraged them to make the most of the opportunity to interact with scientists, explore research laboratories and experience the world of health and innovation firsthand.

S.H.I.N.E. invites students of Grades 9 to 12 from government and private schools to apply scientific thinking to real-world public health challenges.

Aligned with India's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, the initiative aims to encourage scientific curiosity for public health solutions among young learners. This year, participation is by invitation, with ICMR laboratories inviting nearby government and private schools to take part in the initiative, reaching an expected 30,000 students.

Over the two days, participating students will take part in a range of interactive activities, including guided laboratory tours, research exhibitions, poster walks, video presentations, and live demonstrations of ongoing scientific work. Students will also have the opportunity to interact directly with ICMR scientists, gaining insight into their research journeys, areas of expertise, and everyday work in public health.

By opening the doors of its institutes and rural research units to young students, S.H.I.N.E. seeks to make science tangible and accessible, showing students how research addresses the health challenges facing their own communities and encouraging them to see a future for themselves in scientific enquiry.

Through this initiative, ICMR reaffirms its commitment to nurturing scientific temper among India's youth and to inspiring the next generation of researchers who will contribute to the country's health and development goals under the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

headline: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches National Scholarship Portal
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches National Scholarship Portal

Over 6,000 Agriculture Students Receive ₹21.35 Crore in Scholarships through NSP-DBT

Shri Chouhan Emphasises Practical Training, Timely Support and Innovation in Agricultural Education

“Examinations, admissions and payments must all happen on time; that is the real test of an effective system”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan*

“In agriculture, real competence comes not just from classrooms but through practical training”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“Fields, farmers and science working together can strengthen India’s food security and self-reliance”:Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, food security, nutrition and farmers’ income security remain priorities in agriculture”:Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Shri Chouhan Appeals to Agriculture Students to Undertake Plantation Drives at ICAR Institutions Nationwide on Hariyali Amavasya

10 AUG 2026 8:42PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today released scholarship and fellowship funds for agriculture students across the country through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) at ICAR-IARI, Pusa. Under the initiative, more than 6,000 students received a total of ₹21.35 crore directly through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism.

With the new initiative, agriculture students will now receive their scholarships every month directly through DBT, ensuring timely and hassle-free financial assistance.

Addressing the gathering, Union Agriculture Minister Shri Chouhan said that scholarships are not merely a form of financial assistance but an important means of strengthening agricultural education and connecting it with practical learning and greater opportunities. He said the DBT mechanism will ensure that students receive financial support on time and help eliminate the delays associated with traditional systems.

Addressing the students, Shri Chouhan emphasised the importance of practical training in agricultural education. He said classroom-based learning alone cannot produce good farmers, scientists or agricultural entrepreneurs, and that hands-on training is essential for developing real competence in the agriculture sector. He also urged students to share their suggestions and ideas for improvements in the system.

Shri Chouhan said that under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government is giving priority to food security, nutrition and farmers’ income security in the agriculture sector. Appreciating the contribution of ICAR scientists, he said their research, along with the hard work of farmers, has played a vital role in strengthening the country’s food grain reserves.

The Union Minister encouraged young people to set larger goals beyond their careers and contribute meaningfully to the nation. He urged agriculture students not to limit themselves to seeking employment, but to take a leading role in innovation, startups and research in the agriculture sector.

Shri Chouhan said the NSP-DBT system will make scholarship distribution more transparent, faster and seamless. Timely financial assistance will enable students to focus more effectively on their education. He also emphasised that agricultural education must be integrated with technology, training and industry orientation to better address the challenges of the future.

On the occasion of Hariyali Amavasya, Shri Chouhan also appealed to agriculture students at ICAR institutions across the country to participate in plantation drives. He said that green initiatives are part of a collective responsibility towards both agriculture and the environment.

Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, ICAR Director General Dr. M.L. Jat, ICAR Secretary Shri Gyanendra Tripathi, DDG Dr. Yashpal Singh Malik and IARI Director Dr. C. Srinivasa Rao were present at the programme.

Senior officials and scientists from ICAR and IARI, along with a large number of students, attended the programme in person, while thousands of students also joined virtually.

headline: PSB Confluence on 17-18 August to Bring Together Leadership of Public Sector Banks and Financial Institutions for Action-Oriented Dialogue
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

PSB Confluence on 17-18 August to Bring Together Leadership of Public Sector Banks and Financial Institutions for Action-Oriented Dialogue

Union Finance Minister Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman and Minister of State for Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary to address the Two-day Conclave

Participating Institutions to Brainstorm on Identified Themes, Share Proven Practices, and Discuss Practical Initiatives that can be Adopted Across the Banking Ecosystem

10 AUG 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, is set to host PSB Confluence, a two-day ideation conclave scheduled to be held on 17-18 August, in New Delhi, bringing together the leadership of Public Sector Banks (PSBs) and Public Financial Institutions (PFIs). The event aims to foster collaborative dialogue, exchange best practices, and chart out actionable, time-bound strategies with a strong focus on people-centric outcomes.

The event will be graced by the presence of the Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, and Minister of State for Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary.

The PSB Confluence will serve as a platform for participating institutions to brainstorm on identified themes , share proven practices, and discuss practical initiatives that can be adopted across the banking ecosystem.

Deliberations at the conclave will be organised around different thematic tracks, each coordinated by a designated group of institutions. The thematic tracks will focus on Deposit Mobilization, Banking for Youth, Supporting the Investment Cycle, supporting Global Capability Centres, Agriculture & Horticulture Value Chain Infrastructure, Re-imagining the Credit Card Business, and Priority Sector Lending.

The themes have been selected for their direct bearing on citizen welfare and inclusive economic development. The discussions are expected to cover strengthening the resource base available for affordable credit, facilitation of the investment cycle for timely execution of infrastructure projects, development of capability centre ecosystems, strengthening rural value-chain infrastructure to address post-harvest requirements and market linkages, priority sector lending to extend formal credit to underserved segments, and designing banking products to meet the needs of the youth.

Collectively, these themes have been identified for their potential to translate institutional and policy interventions into measurable, people-centric outcomes.

The PSB Confluence will bring together approximately 125 participants,including Chairmen, Managing Directors and Executive Directors of PSBs, and PFIs such as NABARD, EXIM Bank, SIDBI, NHB, IIFCL, IFCI, and NaBFID, alongside senior officials from the Indian Banks Association and the Department of Financial Services.

headline: National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories Launches India’s First Accreditation Scheme for Mobile Food Testing Laboratories
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories Launches India’s First Accreditation Scheme for Mobile Food Testing Laboratories

Multilateral MoU Exchange Strengthens Regulatory Convergence and Integrated Quality Infrastructure

10 AUG 2026 7:48PM by PIB Delhi

The National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), a constituent board of the Quality Council of India (QCI), launched India’s first-of-its-kind Accreditation Scheme for Mobile Food Testing Laboratories under the Integrated Assessment Programme at the ‘Gunvatta Samanvaya – A Multilateral MoU Exchange Ceremony’ held at Hotel Ashoka, New Delhi.

The initiative aims to expand access to reliable, quality-assured and internationally benchmarked food testing services closer to communities. The event also witnessed a Multilateral MoU Exchange among participating organisations, reinforcing efforts towards greater regulatory convergence, coordinated assessments and a more integrated and efficient quality infrastructure.

Secretary, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Shri Amardeep Singh Bhatia, along with senior officials from QCI, NABL, regulatory authorities and commodity boards associated with the Integrated Assessment Framework (IAF), attended the event.

The Accreditation Scheme, developed by NABL, establishes a framework for mobile food testing laboratories to provide reliable, quality-assured and internationally benchmarked testing services closer to communities. By extending accredited food testing beyond conventional laboratory settings, the initiative is expected to strengthen food safety surveillance, improve access to quality testing, support faster regulatory interventions and enhance consumer confidence.

The Multilateral MoU Exchange brought participating organisations together to reaffirm their commitment towards coordinated assessments, regulatory harmonisation and strengthening the Integrated Assessment Framework. The initiative seeks to reduce duplication in assessment processes, promote mutual recognition, improve regulatory efficiency and facilitate ease of doing business while maintaining high standards of quality and compliance.

Addressing the gathering, Secretary, DPIIT, Shri Amardeep Singh Bhatia, underscored the importance of embedding quality across the entire value chain. He stated that initiatives such as ‘Gunvatta Samanvaya’ would contribute to India’s growth journey towards 2047 by promoting quality-led practices.

headline: PM-YASASVI Scheme Implementation in Maharashtra Reviewed Regularly; Corrective Measures Undertaken to Improve Scholarship Coverage
fullText:

PM-YASASVI Scheme Implementation in Maharashtra Reviewed Regularly; Corrective Measures Undertaken to Improve Scholarship Coverage

₹1,940 Lakh Released Under Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme in Maharashtra During 2025-26

10 AUG 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has stated that the implementation of the PM-YASASVI umbrella Scheme in Maharashtra is regularly reviewed through monthly video conferences as well as regional and national-level conferences.

The written reply was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B L Verma in response to questions by Shri Bhaskar Murlidhar Bhagare, Smt Supriya Sule, Prof Varsha Eknath Gaikwad, Shri Mohite Patil Dhairyasheel Rajsinh and Dr Amol Ramsing Kolhe in the Lok Lok Sabha.

The PM-YASASVI umbrella Scheme comprises the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs and others, the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs and others, Top Class Education in Schools for OBCs and others, and Top Class Education in Colleges for OBCs and others.

The Minister said that for the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes, the Central Government provides funds to the implementing States and Union Territories on the basis of approved notional allocation, while selection, verification and disbursement of scholarships to eligible beneficiaries are carried out by the respective States and Union Territories.

Shri Verma stated that Maharashtra was onboarded on the National Scholarship Portal for both the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric OBC Scholarship Schemes from the Academic Year 2025-26 onwards.

As per the information provided, during FY 2025-26, 1,079 applications were received under the PM-YASASVI Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students in Maharashtra. Of these, 1,072 applications were Aadhaar verified and 575 applications were verified.

Under the PM-YASASVI Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students, 1,971 applications were received during FY 2025-26. Of these, 1,965 were Aadhaar verified and 576 applications were verified.

The Minister further stated that the Government released ₹555.74 lakh to the State Government of Maharashtra under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students during 2024-25, increasing to ₹1,940 lakh during 2025-26. No proposal was received from the State in FY 2023-24 and, therefore, no funds were released during that year.

For the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme, no Central Assistance was released during the last three financial years. The reply stated that this was due to non-receipt of proposals in FY 2023-24, pending unutilised balance in the State's SNA account in FY 2024-25, and a technical issue in disbursing funds by the State Government of Maharashtra during FY 2025-26.

Under the Top Class Education in Schools Scheme for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs, 3,470 fresh applications were received in 2023-24, of which 2,324 were finally verified. In 2024-25, 2,192 fresh applications were received, with 1,195 finally verified. In 2025-26, 8,402 fresh applications were received, of which 4,533 were finally verified.

Funds released to Maharashtra under the Top Class Education in Schools Scheme increased from ₹52.31 lakh in 2023-24 to ₹258.55 lakh in 2024-25 and ₹509.37 lakh in 2025-26.

Under the Top Class Education in Colleges Scheme for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs, 363 fresh applications were received and 342 were finally verified in 2023-24. In 2024-25, 731 fresh applications were received, with 611 finally verified.

Funds released under the Top Class Education in Colleges Scheme increased from ₹1,000.39 lakh in 2023-24 to ₹2,712.14 lakh in 2024-25 and ₹2,857.95 lakh in 2025-26.

The Minister stated that necessary corrective measures have been undertaken to address the issue of low scholarship coverage in Maharashtra. These include creating awareness about the Scheme among eligible beneficiaries, coordinating closely with educational institutions and district authorities to improve outreach, and regularly monitoring the application and verification process to ensure timely and accurate disbursal.

The Government has also stated that delays in disbursal mainly arise from incomplete proposals submitted by States/Union Territories, non-submission of Utilisation Certificates against funds already released, non-onboarding of certain States/Union Territories on the SNA-SPARSH platform and non-seeding of bank accounts with Aadhaar. States and Union Territories have been mandated to onboard the SNA-SPARSH platform to improve efficiency and transparency in fund disbursal through real-time, utilisation-based tracking of funds.

The Government continues to pursue timely submission of proposals and Utilisation Certificates through regional and national-level review meetings and video conferences, with a focus on improving outreach, verification and timely scholarship disbursal under PM-YASASVI in Maharashtra.

headline: 2,824 Children Identified, Rescued and Rehabilitated under SMILE Scheme
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

2,824 Children Identified, Rescued and Rehabilitated under SMILE Scheme

1,549 Children Reunited with Parents/Families; 676 Admitted to Schools and 309 to Anganwadi Centres

10 AUG 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has informed the Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the Central Sector Scheme, Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) – Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging, since 23rd October 2023 in 216 major cities and towns across 33 States/Union Territories.

This information was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B L Verma in response to a question by Dr Mohammad Jawed in Lok Sabha.

Under the Scheme, data relating to persons, including children, identified as engaged in the act of begging is collected during surveys and rescue operations undertaken by the Implementing Authorities.

Shri Verma said the Scheme accords special attention to children identified as engaged in the act of begging. Such children are reunited with their families, wherever feasible, or provided appropriate support through Anganwadi Centres and Schools. Children requiring institutional care are produced before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) and linked to Child Care Institutions (CCIs) under the provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the Minister further stated in the House.

As on 30 June 2026, a total of 2,824 children have been identified, rescued and rehabilitated under the Scheme. Of these, 1,549 children have been reunited with their parents/families, 309 children have been admitted to Anganwadi Centres, 290 children have been produced before the Child Welfare Committee, and 676 children have been admitted to Schools.

The Government has stated that age-wise and gender-wise data of identified children are not maintained separately under the Scheme.

The Government is not implementing any scheme specifically for children engaged in the act of begging. However, the SMILE – Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging contains specific provisions for the identification, rescue, rehabilitation and mainstreaming of children engaged in begging through family reunification, admission to schools and Anganwadi Centres, or institutional care through Child Welfare Committees and Child Care Institutions, wherever required.

The Scheme has specific and focused provisions for rehabilitation of children engaged in begging. Its framework provides for 100 per cent rehabilitation and mainstreaming of children surveyed, profiled and rescued from beggary.

The Government has further stated that, since the ongoing SMILE Scheme has a specific focus on the rehabilitation and mainstreaming of children rescued from beggary, there is no need for a separate scheme for this purpose.

As per the State-wise details, Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number with 927 children identified and rehabilitated, followed by Chandigarh with 313, Delhi with 233, Maharashtra with 208 and Andhra Pradesh with 191.

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Removal of Invasive Foreign Species in Reserved Forests

10 AUG 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and its line institutions, actively identify and monitor Invasive Alien Plant Species (IAPS). For identification of invasive species, a separate album of 45 major invasive species has been prepared by Forest Survey of India (FSI). According to FSI, invasive plants show a very dense to a moderate-to-dense and scanty occurrence in the Reserved Forest Areas. Botanical Survey of India (BSI) has recently prepared and submitted a comprehensive, state-wise inventory of potential invasive species spreading across forest and non-forest areas to the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) to facilitate preparation of the National Management Plan of Invasive Species.

The management and removal of invasive plant species and cultivation of indigenous plant species in Reserved Forests and other protected forest areas are undertaken by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations and concerned agencies, in accordance with local requirements and the provisions of the approved forest and wildlife management plans.

The Government promotes conservation, regeneration and enrichment of indigenous/native tree species through sustainable forest management practices. The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages maintenance of environmental stability, restoration of ecological balance and increasing forest/tree cover through afforestation and regeneration using native/indigenous species. Further, the National Working Plan Code, 2023 provides for ecosystem-based forest management, including invasive species management restoration of degraded forest landscapes, soil and moisture conservation measures, watershed management and preference for site-specific indigenous/native species in regeneration and restoration activities, taking into account local ecological conditions. These measures contribute to improving soil moisture, groundwater recharge, water retention and overall ecosystem resilience.

This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

Ministry of MSME and DPIIT sign Memorandum of Understanding to accelerate commercialisation and global market access of India's Geographical Indication (GI) products

'Bharat GI' Banner Launched: Ministry of MSME and DPIIT to Bring Regional GI Products to ONDC and GeM

11 AUG 2026 11:55AM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards unlocking the economic potential of India's rich heritage of Geographical Indication (GI) products, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 05th August,2026 at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The MoU was signed by Md. Salik Parwaiz, Director, Ministry of MSME and Shri Karan Thapar, Director, IPR Division, DPIIT, in the presence of senior officials of both organisations.

DPIIT is the nodal department for the registration and legal protection of Geographical Indications in India under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, while Ministry of MSME is the nodal ministry for steering the growth, financial health and overall development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, traditional industries and artisans across the country. Both sides recognise that while the legal registration of GIs protects regional identity, maximising their economic value requires a coordinated effort to transition these products from localised crafts into scalable, commercially viable and export-ready enterprises. The MoU accordingly establishes a collaborative framework to accelerate the commercialisation, quality standardisation and market penetration of Indian GI products, thereby enhancing the livelihoods of indigenous artisans, weavers and producers, while also strengthening the One District One Product (ODOP) ecosystem in the country.

As joint initiatives, both organisations will work towards integrating ODOP in their programme design and interventions, collaboratively facilitate the onboarding of GI collectives and authorised users onto the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) and the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) under a dedicated “Bharat GI” banner, and co-sponsor dedicated GI Pavilions at national and international trade expos, buyer-seller meets and exhibitions for domestic and global marketing of GI products.

The MoU represents a significant step towards aligning the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade’s (DPIIT) mandate for intellectual property protection with the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises’ (MSME) mandate for enterprise development. The collaboration is expected to strengthen India’s Geographical Indications (GI) ecosystem by facilitating capacity building, digital enablement and enhanced market access for artisans, weavers and producer collectives. It will further support the integration of GI products with premium domestic and international markets, contributing to the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Vocal for Local.

headline: Container Manufacturing Assistance Scheme: Building India's Maritime Future
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Container Manufacturing Assistance Scheme: Building India's Maritime Future

11 AUG 2026 10:42AM by PIB Delhi

India's growing trade and manufacturing ambitions have increased the need for a strong domestic container manufacturing base. The proposed Container Manufacturing Assistance Scheme (CMAS), backed by a ₹10,000 crore outlay, seeks to promote manufacturing, investment and technology development across the container ecosystem. With broader reforms in shipping, ports and logistics, the initiative is expected to strengthen India’s maritime capabilities, generate employment and support India's long-term trade competitiveness.

The Need for Domestic Container Manufacturing

Global trade today is increasingly driven by containerised logistics. According to the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), around 80% of global merchandise trade by volume is transported by sea. Maritime transport forms the backbone of international commerce. Meanwhile, containerised cargo accounts for nearly two-thirds of the value of international trade. These trends highlight the strategic importance of efficient container logistics in supporting global supply chains.

In recent years, geopolitical tensions, supply-chain disruptions and changing shipping routes have exposed vulnerabilities in the global movement of goods. UNCTAD has observed that these disruptions have contributed to freight-rate volatility and increased pressure on maritime transport networks. As a result, many countries are placing greater emphasis on enhancing domestic manufacturing capabilities for critical logistics assets, including shipping containers.

India's growing role in global manufacturing and international trade has significantly increased the demand for containerized cargo movement. However, despite expanding export-import (EXIM) trade and rapid logistics development, India has largely depended on imported empty containers. India imports nearly 2 million empty containers every year to meet domestic demand and for repositioning purposes. This has made container availability vulnerable to global market fluctuations, freight volatility and supply-chain disruptions.

Recognizing these emerging challenges, the Government announced the Container Manufacturing Assistance Scheme (CMAS). It aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India by promoting domestic manufacturing and encouraging investment across the value chain. The initiative also seeks to reduce import dependence and strengthen supply-chain resilience. Further, it complements the Government's initiatives under Make in India, Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 and multimodal logistics development, contributing to India's long-term maritime and trade ambitions.

What are Containers? Shipping containers are standardized steel freight containers used to transport cargo across ships, railways and road vehicles without unloading and repacking the goods during transit. Built to internationally recognised ISO (International Organization for Standardization) specifications, they enable seamless intermodal transport and efficient global trade. The most common sizes are 20-foot and 40-foot containers, measured in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs), the standard unit used to measure container capacity.

What is Container Manufacturing Assistance Scheme (CMAS)?

CMAS was announced in the Union Budget 2026–27. It is a targeted initiative to establish a competitive domestic container manufacturing industry through financial and institutional support.

With an outlay of ₹10,000 crore over five years, the proposed scheme supports establishment of new manufacturing facilities and expansion of existing units. It also aims to enhance manufacturing capacity to meet India's growing demand for shipping containers.

The initiative targets an annual domestic manufacturing capacity of around 10 times the existing container production capacity upto 7.5 lakh Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs). It is expected to generate a market opportunity of nearly ₹80000 lakh crore while positioning India as a reliable producer of internationally competitive shipping containers.

To strengthen the container manufacturing value chain, the scheme provides:

Capital assistance for establishing new Greenfield manufacturing facilities.

Support for expansion of existing Brownfield manufacturing units.

Operational support to improve the competitiveness of domestic container manufacturing.

Support for testing infrastructure, skilling initiatives and capacity building.

Building an Integrated Maritime Ecosystem

CMAS is one element of a broader strategy to build an integrated, domestically anchored container ecosystem. In February 2026, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways signed an MoU to establish the Bharat Container Shipping Line (BCSL). This brings together the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), the Container Corporation of India (CONCOR), the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority, V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority (VOCPA) and the Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SFMCL). The initiative envisages investments of around ₹99,149 crore in fleet development of 51 container vessels of various sizes and domestic container procurement.

This coordinated approach complements the Government's wider logistics initiatives. These include:

· PM Gati Shakti, enhancing connectivity between ports, railways, highways and industrial centres;

· The National Logistics Policy, supporting operational efficiency; and

· The Sagarmala Programme, promoting port-led development.

These initiatives support a resilient and integrated logistics network for India's growing trade volumes.

Employment and Manufacturing Opportunities

Beyond improving logistics resilience, CMAS is expected to generate substantial employment and stimulate industrial development.

It has the potential to generate around 3,000 direct jobs and more than 50,000 indirect jobs across container manufacturing and allied industries.

The initiative is also expected to catalyse growth across several ancillary industries, including:

Recent Progress and Industry Response

In July 2026, India achieved a significant milestone in maritime manufacturing with the rollout of its first India-manufactured export-import (EXIM) shipping container for global shipping company, A.P. Moller–Maersk. The container was unveiled at the Maersk–CONCOR Inland Container Depot in Dadri, Uttar Pradesh.

The container has been manufactured in accordance with internationally recognised ISO standards and the International Convention for Safe Containers (CSC). This makes it suitable for deployment across global shipping networks. The rollout demonstrates India's capability to manufacture globally compliant shipping containers.

Another notable milestone was Maersk's order for 1,000 additional Made-in-India shipping containers with DCM Shriram Group. The order represents an early commercial endorsement of India's emerging manufacturing capability. It also signals growing confidence among global shipping companies in India's ability to produce high-quality shipping containers.

These developments indicate that the Government's policy interventions are beginning to translate into commercial outcomes. They also reinforce India's ambition to emerge as an important manufacturing hub within the global maritime value chain.

Part of Wider Maritime Transformation

CMAS is part of a broader set of reforms strengthening India’s maritime sector. Alongside promoting domestic container production, the Government has introduced a series of legislative, institutional and infrastructure initiatives. Together, these measures seek to modernise India's maritime ecosystem while improving ease of doing business.

These include the enactment of the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, Coastal Shipping Act, 2025 and Indian Ports Act, 2025. These legislations provide an updated legal framework for shipping, coastal trade and port governance. Complementing these reforms are digital initiatives such as the One Nation One Port Process (ONOP), the Maritime Single Window and e-Samudra. These initiatives simplify regulatory procedures, reduce documentation and improve operational efficiency across ports and shipping services.

The Government has also announced a ₹70,000 crore Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Package. The package aims to boost domestic shipbuilding capabilities and encourage greater investments in the maritime manufacturing sector. Along with the proposed Bharat Container Shipping Line (BCSL), these measures seek to build an integrated maritime ecosystem that spans shipbuilding, container manufacturing, shipping services, ports and multimodal logistics.

Major infrastructure projects, including Vadhavan Port, the International Container Transshipment Port at Galathea Bay, the Tuna Tekra Container Terminal and the Outer Harbour Container Terminal at V.O. Chidambaranar Port, are progressing rapidly. These projects are aimed at expanding India's maritime infrastructure and enhance cargo-handling capacity.

Three Indian ports are now ranked among the world's top 30 in the Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) 2025, reflecting continued improvements in port efficiency and reinforcing India's position in global maritime trade.

CMAS marks a significant step towards building a globally competitive maritime manufacturing ecosystem. By promoting container production and reducing dependence on imports, the scheme is expected to strengthen supply-chain resilience, generate employment and enhance India's competitiveness in global trade. Complemented by broader maritime reforms, CMAS has the potential to position India as a leading maritime manufacturing and logistics hub.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam today, highlighting the eight essential qualities that brighten a person's life and build character.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

"अष्टौ गुणाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति प्रज्ञा सुशीलत्वदमौ श्रुतं च।
